definitions.explanation: A particular point in time, or an aspect/characteristic of something.
Used after verbs to indicate timing or circumstances.

examples.japanese: {静|しず}かな{所|ところ}が{好|す}きです。
{今|いま}{食|た}べている{所|ところ}です。
examples.english: I'm in the middle of eating right now.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のいい{所|ところ}は{優|やさ}しいことです。
examples.english: His good point is that he's kind.

examples.japanese: ちょうど{出|で}かける{所|ところ}だったので、{電話|でんわ}に{出|で}られなかった。
examples.english: I was just about to leave, so I couldn't answer the phone.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}から{近|ちか}い{所|ところ}に{住|す}みたいけど、{家賃|やちん}が{高|たか}いのが{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.english: I want to live somewhere close to the station, but the high rent is a problem.

notes: ところ has multiple uses: 1) 'place/location' as a noun, 2) 'aspect/point' when describing characteristics, 3) After verbs: ～ているところ (in the middle of), ～たところ (just did), ～ところ (about to). Written in kanji (所) or hiragana depending on usage.
